correctness.rationale: Proof covers every integer n≥3 and t,B>0. Strict concavity and injectivity establish global uniqueness across independent asymmetric edge weights; matching-preserving automorphisms force the two edge orbits. The four Laplacian eigenvalue blocks yield the exact determinant polynomial; the derived log-derivative is a rational positive-denominator multiple of -Q, and its discriminant/root signs establish the entire threshold and equality case. Exact rational cofactor and independent tree-enumeration checks reproduce the structural identities; finite checks are not used to infer the universal theorem.

originality.rationale: The complete global optimizer and its sharp matching-price elimination threshold are not established in the inspected weighted-tree edge-selection paper or relevant published records. The scalar tree polynomial is a classical eigenvalue consequence, but its optimized threshold across arbitrary per-edge weights and unequal prices is an additional theorem; residual equivalence risk remains.
residual_risks: A historical D-optimal design treatment may specialize to exactly this two-orbit, two-price graph under terminology not recovered by the index.
Classical weighted spanning-tree or crown-graph enumeration could state the two-parameter tree polynomial, which is a proof ingredient but not itself the cost-optimality statement.
Semantic-index and general web searches do not establish priority against unseen archives or unpublished findings.

value.rationale: The weighted spanning-tree enumerator is a justified D-optimal robustness / estimation metric in arXiv:1604.01116. The optimization has a natural independent-conductance price budget on a connected bipartite family; the resulting graph-wide matching deletion occurs at an exact nontrivial price, with unique interior positive allocation from a quadratic, exact optimum, and n-dependent asymptotic shares. These are usable design decisions not supplied by a known unweighted tree table, spectral-gap or trace-inverse optimizer.
